name: Cathedral Glass
summary: A living cathedral window: jewel-tone glass pieces in dark lead came, lit from behind by warm light and coloured rays.
description: The whole world is one backlit stained-glass window. Floor, props, characters, collectibles, icons and even floating numbers are built from the same unit: a glass piece with a luminous off-centre core, a darker rim, faint streaks and a glint, separated by near-black lead came with a soft metallic ridge. Material regions (meadow, autumn leaf carpet, amber path, night glass, clear diamond quarries) are separated by heavier lead, and props cast coloured light pools onto the floor. It feels sacred, festive and handcrafted while staying readable because every figure has a fat lead silhouette.
bestFor: top-down action games with many figures on screen
avoidFor: fast-twitch shooters needing a calm background

difficulty.why: Every new asset has to be cut into glass pieces the way a glazier would (ribs, midribs, folds, facets), drawn in two passes (lead outline, then shaded pieces with inner lead) and given a lit flash copy. Splitting a figure sensibly while keeping it readable on an already busy mosaic floor takes careful design for each new character or prop.

technique.resolution: Native resolution. Actor and prop sprites are baked once at K = clamp(round(screenScale x 1.5), 3, 5) px per world unit; the ground is rendered per pixel in 256-unit chunks at up to 2.5 px per world unit.
technique.summary: Each figure is a list of parts drawn twice: an outline pass fills and strokes every part in lead (one fat outer came), then a fill pass clips glass pieces (BSP-cut polygons, rib lenses, half-leaves) into each part, shades each with an off-centre radial gradient and strokes inner lead. The ground is a per-pixel world-anchored Voronoi with an antialiased lead ramp.
technique.linework: Lead colour #17131c everywhere. Actors: outer came = 0.95 world units each side (lineWidth 1.9), inner lead 0.55 units, part borders 0.66 units, small faces/eyes use ol 0.4-0.6. Floor: piece lead half-width 0.78 units, region-border lead 1.2 units, with a lighter ridge (rgb 84,78,96) along the centre. lineJoin and lineCap round.
technique.shading: Per glass piece: radial gradient from (cx-0.25r, cy-0.3r) to centre, stops 0 = colour mixed 30% with white, 0.48 = base colour (±6% brightness jitter), 1 = colour x0.64. Glowing pieces (faces, eyes, jewels) use 78% warm white core and x0.9 rim. Floor pieces get luminance 0.6 at the lead rising to 0.98 at the centre (smoothstep over 0.34 x cell size).
technique.lighting: Backlit glass: light comes through the window, not from a direction. Warm additive glow sprites behind carved faces, candles and gems; coloured elliptical light pools under props (additive, alpha 0.1-0.3); a screen layer of five coloured diagonal light rays plus a warm centre, added with 'lighter' and slowly drifting.
technique.texture: Cathedral-glass streaks (two curved white strokes at 12% alpha per piece), elliptical glints on half the pieces, sinusoidal ripple banding in floor pieces (±5.5%), seedy bubbles in clear quarries, scattered diagonal white glint strokes on the floor and faint screen-anchored wavy ripple lines.

paletteRules: Every colour is a saturated jewel tone at mid value; pure white and pure black never appear as surface colour (only lead #17131c and highlight mixes).
Lead is the only dark: roughly 12-18% of floor pixels are lead. Never draw a glass piece darker than its colour x0.6.
Background regions use cool or earthy mid tones (greens, crimson, blue, grey); characters use brighter, warmer or paler pieces (orange, ivory, opal, amethyst) so they pop against the floor.
Anything that 'emits' (faces, eyes, flames, gems, cores) uses glow pieces: warm-white core plus an additive glow sprite. Reserve gold/yellow for these and for UI numbers.
Each region picks a random swatch per piece from a 5-7 colour family with ±7% brightness; never use a single flat colour for a whole area.

typography.role: Titles, clock / timer, counters, floating numbers, announcement headings
typography.css: font: 900 34px/1.05 'Cinzel Decorative', 'Cinzel', serif; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #ffdf7e; text-shadow: 2.5px 0 0 #17131c, -2.5px 0 0 #17131c, 0 2.5px 0 #17131c, 0 -2.5px 0 #17131c, 0 0 14px rgba(255,200,90,.7);

typography.role: Body text, labels, bar value text, card descriptions
typography.css: font: 700 11px/1 'Cinzel', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: 3px; color: #cfdaff; text-shadow: 0 1px 2px #17131c;

world.summary: A per-pixel, world-anchored stained-glass floor. Smooth noise fields decide the material region; each material is a jittered-grid Voronoi tessellation (cell 15-30 units) whose seams and region borders become antialiased lead with a metallic ridge. Leaded glass decals (flowers, leaves, stars, roundels) and glints are drawn on top, then prop light pools.
layers: Material field: 5 noise layers sampled on a 4-unit grid, bilinear value / bilinear gradient = signed distance in world units; priority plaza > path (|d| < 21) > night > leaf carpet > meadow.
Voronoi glass per material: meadow cell 20, leaf carpet 15, night 23, path 30 (3 lanes split at ±7 units), plaza = 45° diamond quarries every 17 units.
Per-piece shading: luminance 0.6 at the lead to 0.98 in the middle, sinusoidal streak ±5.5%, macro brightness from a 1150-unit noise.
Lead: piece seams half-width 0.78, region borders 1.2, colour ramp from rgb(28,24,34) at the edge to rgb(84,78,96) at the centre ridge.
Decals: leaded flowers (5 petals) on meadow, autumn leaves on the carpet, gold stars on night glass, amber roundels on the path, seedy bubbles on quarries.
Glints: short diagonal white strokes at 20% alpha scattered every ~24 units.
Prop contact shadows (rgba(16,12,24,0.38)) and additive coloured light pools baked into the chunk.

characters.summary: Chunky, chibi figures (main character drawn x1.15, ~24 units wide and ~42 tall incl. stem) assembled from 10-25 glass pieces: round heads from 5 vertical rib lenses, clothes from BSP-cut mosaics, leaves from two half-pieces split on the midrib, carved faces as glowing gold polygons. Creatures: small root-bulb creatures with jewel caps and ivory bodies, a fast opal floating spirit with a dissolving hem, a large violet-and-brown giant with a ruby core. Pre-rendered in 4 walk frames plus a 'flash' (lit glass) copy of each frame.
rules: Every figure has one fat outer lead came (1.9 units wide) from the outline pass, so silhouettes read on the busy floor.
Faces and eyes are glow pieces (warm-white core) plus an additive glow sprite: the face is the brightest thing on any figure.
Pieces get smaller where detail matters (face, hands) and larger on bodies; never more than ~25 pieces on a small figure. Body pieces 30-80 units², face/detail pieces 3-15 units².
Figures are warmer, paler or more saturated than the floor region they stand on; creature colours (ivory, amethyst, opal) are absent from the floor palettes.
Three distinct creature silhouettes and sizes: small ~26 units tall, floating ~28, large ~64; each anchored by a flat dark ellipse shadow.
Facing = horizontal flip of the baked sprite; carved faces are drawn offset 1.5 units towards the facing side.
Flash = blit the pre-baked flash copy (pieces mixed 58% toward warm white, lead kept) at alpha <= 0.62 over the normal sprite.
Disappearing = the figure shatters into 6-16 leaded shards in its own colours; appearing = shards fly in and assemble.

props.summary: Props are drawn with the same two-pass Painter as the characters: fat lead silhouette, glass pieces with their own gradients, glowing jewel accents. Each prop casts a dark contact shadow and coloured additive light pools onto the floor.
rules: Trees: BSP-cut trunk + 5 foliage lobes (ellipse mosaic + 2-3 leaf pieces each) in autumn, summer or blossom families, with glowing fruit jewels; they sway as a horizontal skew of 0.02 at 1.1 rad/s.
Bushes: 3 lobes + berry jewels; sway skew 0.03.
Gothic arch: stone mosaic frame, jewel-mosaic window (pieces <= 11 units²), mullion and a quatrefoil with a ruby centre; casts red, blue and gold light pools (alpha 0.26).
Candles: ivory pieces + layered flame glow pieces + a flickering warm glow (0.75 + 0.25 sin(11t) sin(7.3t)); warm pool rgb(255,180,70) at 0.3.
Graves: grey mosaic slabs with an inlaid pale-blue glowing cross; cold pool rgb(150,200,255) at 0.12.
Gourds: rib-lens pieces in #c85a14 / #e47820 / #f39232, sometimes carved with a glowing face.
15 prop variants are baked once at init (3 trees, 2 bushes, 2 arches, 2 candle groups, 3 graves, 3 gourd groups).

effects.name: Shatter
effects.how: When a figure disappears, 6 (floating spirit), 8 (small) or 16 (large) shard sprites: 3 baked triangle/quad shapes with lead outline, coloured from the figure palette. They fly out with gravity 300, drag 1.4, life 0.9-1.4 s, spin ±8 rad/s and fake 3D tumble by scaling y with |cos|; when edge-on they flash a glint.

effects.name: Impact glint
effects.how: Four-point star sprite (white core, tinted halo, curved spikes 7.5 units) added with 'lighter', scale ramps in over 30% of life then out; 45% chance of a single shard.

effects.name: Seed projectile
effects.how: A two-piece leaded seed sprite rotated to its heading, y-scale 0.6-1 by spin, with a 16-unit additive tapered trail (rgba 255,214,120 .75 to 0) and a small gold glow.

effects.name: Collectibles
effects.how: A kite split into 4 facets around (0, -1.4), two of them glowing, in aqua (large: gold with a ruby centre); bobs ±1.1 units with an aqua additive halo and a rare twinkle glint.

effects.name: Glow sprites
effects.how: Radial gradients baked once (stops 0:0.9, 0.25:0.45, 0.6:0.12, 1:0 alpha) in warm, gold, aqua, cold and ruby, blitted with globalCompositeOperation 'lighter' behind faces, collectibles, candles and creature cores.

effects.name: Celebration beams
effects.how: 12 vertical light beams (3.2 x 40 units, gradient 0 / 0.7 / 0 with a white 0.8-unit core) in gold, rose, blue and mint around the main character plus a lead-and-gold expanding ellipse ring and 10 glints.

effects.name: Ring shockwave
effects.how: Ellipse ring (ry = 0.45 rx) stroked twice: lead at width w+1.4, then the colour additively at width w = 2.6 x (1-t).

effects.name: Floating numbers
effects.how: Cinzel Decorative 900 at 9.2 units (12.5 for the large variant), stroked twice in lead (width 0.26 x font size, once offset down), filled with a vertical gradient (large #fff6c0 > #ffcf40 > #ff7a1a, small #ffffff > #e6eeff > #a9c0ee), white 50% band over the top; pop 0.4 > 1.25 > 1.

atmosphere.summary: No directional light: the light comes through the glass. Highlights sit at the upper left of every piece, light sources are glow pieces plus additive glow sprites, props cast coloured pools, and a baked window overlay (vignette, lead frame with gold fillet, pane ripples, drifting coloured rays) sits over the whole screen.
rules: Glow sprites: radial gradients with alpha stops 0: .9, .25: .45, .6: .12, 1: 0; warm rgb(255,190,80) r 16, gold rgb(255,210,90) r 10, aqua rgb(110,240,220) r 10, cold rgb(150,200,255) r 14, ruby rgb(255,60,80) r 14; always 'lighter'.
Shadows: flat ellipses rgba(14,10,22,0.42) (floating spirit 0.25); main character 7.5 x 2.4, small creature 8 x 2.6, floating 5 x 1.7, large 19 x 5.5. No directional drop shadows.
Coloured additive light pools under props and a warm pulsing pool (r 20 x 0.4, 0.85 ± 0.15) under the main character.
Vignette like a deep window embrasure: radial from 0.28 H to 0.56 x diagonal, rgba(14,8,26, 0 / .1 @ .55 / .36 @ .85) to rgba(10,6,20,.62).
Window frame (s = H/900): lead stroke 10 s at inset 5 s (rgba(16,12,22,.85)), gold fillet 2 s at inset 11 s (rgba(214,170,80,.35)), dark corner rosettes r 110 s.
70 faint wavy ripple lines (white 2.8% / navy 3%), screen-anchored like real pane distortion.

Light layer at 55% x 50% resolution: warm centre rgba(255,226,170,.16) plus five diagonal coloured rays (rose, gold, blue, amber, lilac) at alpha 0.075 -> 0.028 -> 0, slanted 0.45 H, added with 'lighter', stretched to 110% width and drifting ±2.5% of the width at 0.12 rad/s.

ui.summary: HUD pieces are leaded glass panels: thick lead borders (3-5 px) with a 2 px gold fillet ring, radial-gradient jewel glass fills, gothic arch tops on the clock, counter and choice cards, bars with lead mullions every 40-46 px and a white highlight strip. Text is Cinzel / Cinzel Decorative with a 12-direction lead text-shadow outline.

motion: 4 baked walk frames per figure; main character cycles at 0.42 x distance, small creature at 0.85, large creature at 0.32; frame = floor(phase x 4) & 3.
Main character walk: lift |sin(phase x TAU)| x 2.2 units, rock ±0.05 rad, y-squash ±2%; idle breath ±2.5% y / ∓1.5% x at 3 rad/s.
Small creature hops: lift |sin| x 1.2 units and rocks ±0.09 rad. Floating spirit hovers 4 units up, bobs ±1.5 at 2.4 rad/s, tilts with velocity up to 0.14 rad, 6 fps frames, alpha 0.86.
Large creature stomps: lift 1.8 units, contact squash (1-up)^4 x 5%.
Glows flicker with products of two sines (e.g. sin(9t) x sin(5.3t)); candle flames 0.75 + 0.25 sin(11t) sin(7.3t).
Trees and bushes sway as a horizontal skew of 0.02-0.03 at 1.1 rad/s; the screen light rays drift ±2.5% of the width at 0.12 rad/s.
Flash decays from 1 to 0; disappearing is a 0.22 s flash-copy pop (scale 1 to 1.18, fading) followed by shards; appearing assembles shards over 0.85 s.
do: Draw every figure in two passes: a lead outline pass first, then the glass pieces with inner lead.
Give each glass piece its own off-centre radial gradient (light core, dark rim) and brightness jitter.
Split shapes where a real glazier would: head ribs, leaf midribs, cloak folds, facets of a gem.
Make faces, eyes, flames and jewels glow pieces plus an additive glow sprite.
Anchor the floor tessellation in world space and separate material regions with heavier lead.
Cast coloured additive light pools from props onto the floor.
Pre-bake every sprite and a lit 'flash' copy at init; blit at runtime.
Keep the overlay: vignette, lead window frame with gold fillet and slow coloured light rays.
dont: Don't use flat fills without lead seams; it instantly becomes generic vector art.
Don't flash figures pure white: the flash copy keeps the lead and only lights the glass.
Don't make floor pieces as small as figure pieces; floor cells are 15-30 units, figure pieces 2-8 units.
Don't use thin or coloured outlines; lead is always the same near-black #17131c.
Don't add drop shadows with hard offsets or realistic directional lighting.
Don't use dark or desaturated figure colours on the same-hued region (e.g. green creatures on meadow).
Don't compute the per-pixel ground every frame; bake it in chunks.
performance: All figure/prop/icon sprites (main character 4 frames x2, 3 small-creature variants x4 frames x2, floating spirit and large creature 4x2, props, shards, glows) are baked once at init at 3-5 px per unit. The ground is the hot spot: per-pixel field bilinear + 3x3 Voronoi search + lead ramp, done as a time-sliced generator per 256-unit chunk at up to 2.5 px/unit and cached. Per frame: only drawImage blits, a handful of additive glow blits and two overlay drawImages (overlay baked per screen size, light layer at half resolution). Hundreds of figures are fine because each is one or two blits.
